policy.privacy.lead: This site is built so that reading it tells nobody anything about you.
policy.privacy.collect.title: What this site collects
policy.privacy.collect.p1: Nothing. There are no accounts, no cookies, no advertising and no analytics run by this site. Pages load only this site’s own files, from its own address and its own file store.
policy.privacy.device.title: What stays on your device
policy.privacy.device.p1: Your watchlists, the language and level of detail you chose, and the tips you dismissed are saved in your browser’s storage on your own device. They are never sent anywhere. Clearing your browser’s data for this site removes them.
policy.privacy.device.p2: Files you open in the analysis workbench, and the queries you run there, are processed inside your browser and are not uploaded.
policy.privacy.hosting.title: What the delivery network sees
policy.privacy.hosting.p1: The site is delivered by Cloudflare. As with any website, the network that delivers a page receives your IP address and the address of the page you asked for, in order to send it. Cloudflare shows the site’s maintainers traffic totals. This project keeps no visitor logs of its own.
policy.privacy.hosting.p2: Cloudflare’s network also tries to add its own analytics script to pages. This site’s security policy refuses to load it, so it does not run and sends nothing.
policy.privacy.thirdparty.title: Other websites
policy.privacy.thirdparty.p1: Links to official sources open those organisations’ own websites, which have their own privacy practices. A chart from this site embedded on another website loads only this site’s files.
policy.accessibility.lead: The site aims to be usable by everyone, including people who use a keyboard, a screen reader or high magnification.
policy.accessibility.aim.title: The aim
policy.accessibility.aim.p1: The aim is to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA. This is an aim, not a certified claim: the site has not had an independent audit.
policy.accessibility.works.title: What is in place
policy.accessibility.works.li1: Every page can be used with a keyboard alone, and keyboard focus is always visible.
policy.accessibility.works.li2: Charts and the main maps have a table of the same numbers behind a “View as table” button, and a text description.
policy.accessibility.works.li3: The standard map is a single tab stop: arrow keys move between countries, and the current country and its value are announced.
policy.accessibility.works.li4: Colour is not the only way information is shown, and map colours were checked against common forms of colour-vision deficiency.
policy.accessibility.works.li5: Animation is switched off for people whose device asks for reduced motion.
policy.accessibility.limits.title: Known limits
policy.accessibility.limits.li1: An automated audit of the main pages reports no issues, but the site has not yet been tested by people who use a screen reader every day.
policy.accessibility.limits.li2: On the pan-and-zoom map, countries cannot be chosen with the keyboard. The standard map and the table can be.
policy.accessibility.limits.li3: The Spanish, French and German text is machine-drafted and not yet reviewed, so those languages are not offered in the language menu.
policy.accessibility.limits.li4: The simulation and analysis tools load large files and can be slow on older devices.
policy.accessibility.feedback.title: Tell us what does not work
policy.accessibility.feedback.p1: If something does not work for you, please use the contact details on the About page. Say which page it was and what you were using. Problems reported this way are listed in the public changelog when they are fixed.
policy.corrections.lead: How errors on this site are reported, fixed and recorded.
policy.corrections.principle.title: The source is right
policy.corrections.principle.p1: If a number on this site differs from the official source it came from, the source is right and this site is wrong. Every number links to its source so that anyone can check.
policy.corrections.report.title: Reporting an error
policy.corrections.report.p1: Use “Report an error” on the About page. Say which page, which number, and what the source says. An error in a source’s own figures should be reported to that source: this site can only correct how it reads and presents them.
policy.corrections.process.title: How an error is fixed
policy.corrections.process.p1: A confirmed error is fixed in the code or configuration that produced it, never by editing a number by hand, so the same error cannot come back at the next update.
policy.corrections.process.p2: Published versions of the data are never rewritten. A link to an earlier version keeps showing what the site said then, so a correction is visible rather than silent.
policy.corrections.record.title: The record
policy.corrections.record.p1: Each correction is listed in the public changelog with its date and what changed. Changes to how numbers are calculated are listed there too.
policy.editorial-standards.lead: The rules this site holds itself to.
policy.editorial-standards.publish.title: What is published
policy.editorial-standards.publish.p1: Only figures and notices published by official public sources, such as the World Health Organization and national public-health agencies, and clearly labelled calculations made from them. Each source is listed with its licence on the Sources page.
policy.editorial-standards.never.title: What is never published
policy.editorial-standards.never.li1: A number without a source, or an estimate presented as a report.
policy.editorial-standards.never.li2: Forecasts, projections or early warnings. The teaching simulations are labelled as illustrations and are never fitted to real data.
policy.editorial-standards.never.li4: A rating of how serious an event is. The order of lists follows a published formula based on how recent and how well documented the reports are.
policy.editorial-standards.words.title: Wording
policy.editorial-standards.words.p1: Text written by this site describes what was reported, when and by whom. Words that characterise risk are left to the official sources, whose own phrases are shown in quotation marks.
policy.editorial-standards.automation.p1: Much of this site is produced by programs: counts are read from notices automatically, notices are grouped into events automatically, and summaries are assembled from templates. Anything produced that way is labelled, links to the original notice, and should be checked against it before being quoted.
The site carries no advertising and no sponsored content, and sources have no say over how their figures are presented. Who maintains the site is stated on the About page.
